title: New Zealand Thrash India by 244 Runs to Keep ODI Series Alive
excerpt: Will Young's 125 punished two early drops as New Zealand posted 333 at Bay Oval, before Matt Henry's opening-over burst bowled India out for 89.
body:
• New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday, bowling India out for 89 in 26.4 overs.
  • Will Young, dropped twice on 5 in the second over, made 125 off 108 balls as New Zealand posted 333; Tim Seifert added 58 off 48.
  • Matt Henry took three wickets in the first over of the chase — Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and captain Shreyas Iyer all for ducks — and finished as player of the match.
  • India still lead the five-match series 2-1, with the deciding fifth ODI to come at the same venue.

New Zealand produced the most one-sided result of the series on Friday, defeating India by 244 runs in the fourth one-day international at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui. After posting 333 in their 50 overs, the hosts dismissed India for 89 in 26.4 overs, according to the Cricbuzz scorecard, which named Matt Henry player of the match.

Young makes India pay for two drops

The match turned on an over India will want to forget. In the second over of New Zealand's innings, Will Young, then on five, was dropped twice in consecutive deliveries from Auqib Nabi — first by Rohit Sharma at slip, then by wicketkeeper Ishan Kishan. Young went on to score 125 off 108 balls, with 14 fours and four sixes, his fifth ODI century and his first against India, IANS reported. He reached his hundred off 88 balls in the 32nd over, his first ODI century since making 107 against Pakistan at the 2025 Champions Trophy.

Tim Seifert gave the innings its early pace, scoring 58 off 48 balls with six fours and three sixes. Seifert reached his maiden ODI half-century off 42 balls and, according to IANS, became the first New Zealand batter to reach fifty inside the opening 10 overs of an ODI against India. The opening pair added 85 before Seifert top-edged Gurnoor Brar and Kishan took the catch.

"So to scrap through to 333 I think is a decent score."

— Will Young, New Zealand opener

Late wickets keep New Zealand to 333

Young added 90 for the fourth wicket with Finn Allen, who made 41, before Axar Patel broke the stand. Young's innings ended when substitute fielder Kumar Kushagra held a catch at the second attempt off part-time off-spinner Naman Dhir. Mitchell Santner made 24, Kristian Clarke 22 and Kyle Jamieson finished unbeaten on 19 as New Zealand were bowled out off the final balls of the innings. For India, Axar Patel, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi took two wickets each, while Kuldeep Yadav, playing his first game of the tour, conceded 73 in eight overs without a wicket, IANS reported.

Henry destroys the chase in one over

India's reply collapsed immediately. Chasing 334, India lost Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and captain Shreyas Iyer — all without scoring — in Matt Henry's opening over, according to match reports. Henry went on to take six wickets in the innings, and Matthew Fisher claimed three, as India were dismissed for 89. The defeat was India's heaviest of the series by a wide margin, and it came in a match they had entered needing a win to seal the series with a game to spare.

What it means

India lead the five-match series 2-1 after winning the first two ODIs and seeing the third abandoned because of rain. New Zealand's win keeps the series alive and sends it to a deciding fifth match at the same venue. For diaspora viewers in North America, the decider falls on Sunday, November 15, 2026, per the series schedule reported around the fourth ODI — check local listings on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV, the broadcasters carrying the tour, for start times in your time zone.
